events.title: Council updates the Street Maintenance and Rehabilitation Policy and adopts the Five-Year Paving Plan (Equity Alternative)

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 70,204-N.S. updating the Street Maintenance and Rehabilitation Policy and the Five-Year Paving Plan "Equity Alternative", amended to approve the first three years of the plan, with the condition that its criteria would not govern funds from potential future ballot measures; staff to return in January 2024.

citations.quote: Paving Plan Equity Alternative amended to approve the first three years of the plan

value.basis: programmed annual paving funding, all sources (FY2023-FY2027 plan)
value.source: gas tax $495,303; Measure BB $2,700,000; Measure F $155,000; Capital Improvement Fund (General Fund) $1,925,000; SB1 $2,000,000; plus Measure T1 $6.9M and a $1.2M federal grant

purpose.value: Staff projected that at the budgeted baseline "the PCI will drop to 52 by the year 2023"; the Public Works Commission projected citywide PCI of 49.1 by 2027 at the current level of investment. Both plans were designed within the same funding.

citations.quote: the PCI will drop to 52 by the year 2023

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the Public Works Commission recommended a different plan, version 12A ("Arterial Alternative"), and a Councilmember-authored policy update was also on the agenda. Council adopted the Equity Alternative instead.

actual.needed: Paving delivered under this plan, by year

outcomes.needed: Whether the January 2024 policy update came back as directed

outstanding.needed: No financial commitment stated in the record we hold.

uncertainties: The record does not list individual names for "All Ayes" votes.

competing_proposals.name: Equity Alternative (staff recommendation; adopted, first three years)
competing_proposals.mix: Arterials 1.18 mi, collectors 4.06 mi, residential 10.70 mi; Equity Zone 5.21 mi
competing_proposals.expected_outcome: No separate PCI projection for this plan in the record; staff projected the network PCI would fall at the budgeted funding level.
competing_proposals.funding_restrictions: Same sources and amounts as the other plan ($7,275,303 a year plus T1 and a grant).
competing_proposals.tradeoff_as_documented: Staff: "These investments are offset by a corresponding reduction of investment in arterials."

citations.quote: These investments are offset by a corresponding reduction of investment in arterials

competing_proposals.name: Arterial Alternative, Plan 12A (Public Works Commission recommendation; not adopted)
competing_proposals.mix: Arterials 5.99 mi, collectors 4.12 mi, residential 5.38 mi; Equity Zone 2.19 mi
competing_proposals.expected_outcome: Commission: citywide PCI 49.1 by 2027 "at the current level of investment" (applies to the funding level, not to this plan alone).
competing_proposals.tradeoff_as_documented: Staff: the plan "does not address equity, does much less for residential streets generally". Commission: focuses on "long contiguous stretches of paving on the primary transportation network".

citations.quote: does not address equity, does much less for residential streets generally
focusing on long contiguous stretches of paving on the primary transportation network

events.title: Council commits $8 million a year more of General Fund money to street maintenance

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 70,456-N.S., a fiscal policy allocating $8 million a year from the General Fund to street maintenance on top of the existing $7.3 million, $15.3 million in all, adjusted for inflation. It may be suspended in a year Council draws $1 million or more from the Stabilization Reserve to adopt a budget, or by a two-thirds vote of Council.

citations.quote: existing General Fund street paving budget of $7.3 million
a two-thirds vote of the City Council
allocate $8 million annually in General Fund monies for street maintenance

purpose.value: "This policy is needed to ensure that deferred street maintenance is supported by an ongoing adequate General Fund contribution."

citations.quote: ensure that deferred street maintenance is supported by an

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the policy itself sets two ways to suspend it (a Stabilization Reserve draw of $1 million or more, or a two-thirds vote). No alternative funding level was voted on in the record we hold.

citations.quote: a two-thirds vote of the City Council

actual.needed: General Fund paving appropriations and actual expenditures each year since FY2023

outcomes.value: City staff (July 2026): about 29.4 centerline miles paved in FY2024-FY2026, against a historical average of about 2 to 3 miles a year, an acceleration staff attribute to "the commitment of additional General Fund resources in 2022". This is the City's attribution, not a BeTH finding.

citations.quote: This acceleration was made possible by the commitment of additional General Fund

outstanding.value: Carried into Measure FF: voters made the $15.3 million (inflation-adjusted) non-FF street budget a condition of collecting the tax (BMC 7.11.030(B)).

uncertainties: Whether every year since FY2023 met the $15.3 million (adjusted) level is not yet established.
The record does not list individual names for "All Ayes" votes; two members arrived after roll call and the agenda does not say whether they were present for this item.
